category: Visual LISP Curve Functions, Reactors & Namespaces
description: The vlax-curve- geometry functions that measure and evaluate lines, arcs, circles, ellipses, polylines and splines; the vlr- reactor functions that run AutoLISP callbacks on object, command, drawing, document and system-variable events; and the functions that share data across document namespaces, persist LISP data in drawings, automate other COM applications and register commands. All require (vl-load-com) and are Windows only.

tools.name: vlax-curve-getStartPoint
tools.description: Returns the WCS start point of a curve entity (line, arc, circle, ellipse, polyline, spline, ray, xline). For closed curves the start and end points coincide. Accepts either an entity name or a VLA-object, like all vlax-curve- functions.

parameters.name: curve-obj
parameters.description: Entity name or VLA-object of a curve.

tools.example:
(setq e (car (entsel "\nSelect curve: ")))
(setq sp (vlax-curve-getStartPoint e)
      ep (vlax-curve-getEndPoint e))
(command "_.TEXT" sp 2.5 0 "S")
tools.notes: Returns nil for non-curve entities. For a circle the start point is at angle 0 of its OCS.

tools.name: vlax-curve-getEndPoint
tools.description: Returns the WCS endpoint of a curve. Together with getStartPoint it is used to chain, reverse-check or connect polylines and lines without parsing DXF codes.

parameters.name: curve-obj
parameters.description: Entity name or VLA-object of a curve.

tools.example:
(if (equal (vlax-curve-getEndPoint e1) (vlax-curve-getStartPoint e2) 1e-6)
  (princ "\nCurves are connected end-to-start."))
tools.notes: Always compare points with (equal p1 p2 fuzz), never with =.

tools.name: vlax-curve-getStartParam
tools.description: Returns the parameter value at the start of a curve. Parameters are the internal curve coordinate: for polylines each vertex is an integer parameter, for arcs and circles the parameter is the angle in radians, for lines it equals the distance.

parameters.name: curve-obj
parameters.description: Entity name or VLA-object of a curve.

tools.example:
(setq p0 (vlax-curve-getStartParam e)
      p1 (vlax-curve-getEndParam e))
(princ (strcat "\nParameter range: " (rtos p0 2 3) " - " (rtos p1 2 3)))
tools.notes: Normally 0.0 but not guaranteed (arcs start at their start angle), so always query it instead of assuming.

tools.name: vlax-curve-getEndParam
tools.description: Returns the parameter value at the end of a curve. For an LWPOLYLINE it equals the number of segments, which makes it the standard way to count polyline segments or iterate vertices by integer parameter.

parameters.name: curve-obj
parameters.description: Entity name or VLA-object of a curve.

tools.example:
; list all vertices of a polyline
(setq i 0 n (fix (vlax-curve-getEndParam pl)) pts nil)
(while (<= i n)
  (setq pts (cons (vlax-curve-getPointAtParam pl i) pts) i (1+ i)))
(reverse pts)
tools.notes: For a closed polyline the last parameter returns to the first vertex, so skip the final point if you want unique vertices.

tools.name: vlax-curve-getDistAtPoint
tools.description: Returns the length along a curve from its start to a given point that lies on the curve. Used for chainage/station calculations along alignments, pipes and cable routes.

parameters.name: point
parameters.description: WCS point on the curve.

tools.example:
(setq pick (getpoint "\nPoint near route: ")
      onc  (vlax-curve-getClosestPointTo route (trans pick 1 0))
      ch   (vlax-curve-getDistAtPoint route onc))
(princ (strcat "\nChainage: " (rtos ch 2 3)))
tools.notes: Returns nil if the point is not exactly on the curve; snap it first with vlax-curve-getClosestPointTo. Points from getpoint are UCS and must be converted with trans.

tools.name: vlax-curve-getPointAtDist
tools.description: Returns the WCS point located a given distance along a curve from its start. It is the basis of custom MEASURE/DIVIDE style routines that place blocks, ticks or labels at regular chainages.

parameters.name: distance
parameters.description: Distance from the start, between 0 and the curve length.

tools.example:
(setq len (vlax-curve-getDistAtParam pl (vlax-curve-getEndParam pl)) d 0.0)
(while (<= d len)
  (entmake (list '(0 . "POINT") (cons 10 (vlax-curve-getPointAtDist pl d))))
  (setq d (+ d 25.0)))
tools.notes: Returns nil for distances outside the curve length. Total length is (vlax-curve-getDistAtParam c (vlax-curve-getEndParam c)).

tools.name: vlax-curve-getParamAtPoint
tools.description: Returns the curve parameter at a point that lies on the curve. For polylines the integer part identifies the segment index, which is how routines find which segment the user clicked.

parameters.name: point
parameters.description: WCS point on the curve.

tools.example:
(setq sel (entsel "\nPick polyline segment: ")
      pl  (car sel)
      pt  (vlax-curve-getClosestPointTo pl (trans (cadr sel) 1 0))
      seg (fix (vlax-curve-getParamAtPoint pl pt)))
(princ (strcat "\nSegment index: " (itoa seg)))
tools.notes: Returns nil for points not on the curve. Use (vla-GetBulge pl seg) afterwards to test whether the segment is an arc.

tools.name: vlax-curve-getPointAtParam
tools.description: Returns the WCS point at a given parameter along a curve. With integer parameters on polylines it returns vertices; with fractional values it interpolates along the segment (for example 2.5 is the midpoint of segment 2).

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: Parameter between start and end parameter.

tools.example:
; midpoint of every polyline segment
(repeat (setq i (fix (vlax-curve-getEndParam pl)))
  (setq i (1- i))
  (print (vlax-curve-getPointAtParam pl (+ i 0.5))))
tools.notes: Parameter spacing is not proportional to length for splines and ellipses; use getPointAtDist for equal spacing.

tools.name: vlax-curve-getClosestPointTo
tools.description: Returns the point on a curve nearest to a given point, optionally allowing the curve to be extended. It is used to project picked points onto curves before calling the distance and parameter functions, and for perpendicular-foot calculations.

parameters.name: given-pnt
parameters.description: WCS point to project.

parameters.name: extend
parameters.description: If non-nil, the curve is treated as extended beyond its ends.

tools.example:
(setq p  (trans (getpoint "\nPoint: ") 1 0)
      on (vlax-curve-getClosestPointTo crv p))
(princ (strcat "\nOffset from curve: " (rtos (distance p on) 2 3)))
tools.notes: Works in 3D; for a 2D projection onto a plane use vlax-curve-getClosestPointToProjection.

tools.name: vlax-curve-getFirstDeriv
tools.description: Returns the first derivative (tangent direction vector) of a curve at a parameter, in WCS. Its angle gives the tangent direction, used to rotate blocks or text so that they follow a path.

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: Parameter at which to evaluate the derivative.

tools.example:
(setq par (vlax-curve-getParamAtPoint crv pt)
      d   (vlax-curve-getFirstDeriv crv par)
      ang (angle '(0 0 0) d))
(vla-InsertBlock ms (vlax-3d-point pt) "ARROW" 1 1 1 ang)
tools.notes: The vector length is not normalised. vlax-curve-getSecondDeriv returns the second derivative (curvature direction).

tools.name: vlax-curve-getArea
tools.description: Returns the area enclosed by a closed curve (circle, ellipse, closed polyline, closed spline). For open curves the area is computed as if the curve were closed by a straight segment. Faster and scriptable compared with the AREA command.

parameters.name: curve-obj
parameters.description: Entity name or VLA-object of a curve.

tools.example:
(setq ss (ssget '((0 . "LWPOLYLINE") (70 . 1))) i -1 tot 0.0)
(while (setq e (ssname ss (setq i (1+ i))))
  (setq tot (+ tot (vlax-curve-getArea e))))
(princ (strcat "\nTotal area: " (rtos tot 2 2)))
tools.notes: Self-intersecting polylines give meaningless results. Use the Area property of regions or hatches for areas with holes.

tools.name: vlax-curve-isClosed
tools.description: Returns T if the curve's start point equals its endpoint (closed), nil otherwise. Circles and closed polylines return T; a polyline whose last vertex merely coincides with the first also returns T even if its Closed flag is off.

parameters.name: curve-obj
parameters.description: Entity name or VLA-object of a curve.

tools.example:
(if (not (vlax-curve-isClosed pl))
  (princ "\nBoundary is open - cannot compute area."))
tools.notes: Related predicates: vlax-curve-isPlanar and vlax-curve-isPeriodic.

tools.name: vlr-object-reactor
tools.description: Creates an object reactor that fires callbacks when one or more owner objects are modified, copied, erased, unerased or closed. Commonly used to keep associated objects in sync, such as a label that follows a line. The callback receives the notifying object, the reactor and a parameter list.

parameters.name: owners
parameters.description: List of VLA-objects that trigger the reactor.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Any application data stored with the reactor (retrieve with vlr-data).

parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: List of (event-name . callback-function) pairs, e.g. (:vlr-modified . my-mod), (:vlr-erased . my-erase).

tools.example:
(defun on-mod (owner rea args)
  (princ (strcat "\nLength now " (rtos (vla-get-Length owner) 2 2))))
(setq ln (vlax-ename->vla-object (car (entsel))))
(vlr-object-reactor (list ln) "len-watch" '((:vlr-modified . on-mod)))
tools.notes: A callback must not modify its owner object (the object is open for notification) and must not call (command); queue the work in a command-ended reactor instead. Other events: :vlr-cancelled, :vlr-copied, :vlr-goodbye, :vlr-openedForModify, :vlr-subObjModified, :vlr-modifiedXData, :vlr-objectClosed.

tools.name: vlr-command-reactor
tools.description: Creates an editor reactor that notifies of command events: a command starting, ending, being cancelled or failing, and unknown commands. Typical uses are enforcing layer standards (switch layer before HATCH or DIM commands), logging and post-processing objects after a command completes.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Application data or nil.

parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: Pairs such as (:vlr-commandWillStart . fn), (:vlr-commandEnded . fn), (:vlr-commandCancelled . fn), (:vlr-commandFailed . fn), (:vlr-unknownCommand . fn).

tools.example:
(defun hatch-layer (rea cmd)
  (if (wcmatch (car cmd) "*HATCH")
    (setvar "CLAYER" "HATCH")))
(if (not *hatch-rea*)
  (setq *hatch-rea* (vlr-command-reactor nil '((:vlr-commandWillStart . hatch-layer)))))
tools.notes: The callback receives (reactor command-list) where (car command-list) is the command name in upper case. Guard creation with a global so reloading the file does not create duplicate reactors.

tools.name: vlr-editor-reactor
tools.description: Creates a legacy general editor reactor that can receive the AutoCAD R14-era editor events (commands, LISP, drawing open/save, system variables and others) in one reactor object. Since AutoCAD 2000 the events are split into specific reactor types, which should be preferred for new code.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Application data or nil.

parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: List of (event . function) pairs for the supported editor events.

tools.example: (vlr-editor-reactor nil '((:vlr-commandEnded . my-cmd-ended)))
tools.notes: Kept for backward compatibility; events introduced after R14 cannot be referenced through :VLR-Editor-Reactor. Use vlr-command-reactor, vlr-dwg-reactor, vlr-sysvar-reactor and friends instead.

tools.name: vlr-dwg-reactor
tools.description: Creates an editor reactor that notifies of drawing-file events such as beginning or completing a save, beginning to close, and opening a drawing. Used for automatic tasks like stamping a save date, purging or exporting a PDF on save.

parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: Pairs such as (:vlr-beginSave . fn), (:vlr-saveComplete . fn), (:vlr-beginClose . fn), (:vlr-databaseToBeDestroyed . fn), (:vlr-dwgFileOpened . fn).

tools.example:
(defun stamp-save (rea args)
  (setvar "USERS5" (menucmd "M=$(edtime,$(getvar,date),YYYY-MO-DD HH:MM)")))
(vlr-dwg-reactor nil '((:vlr-beginSave . stamp-save)))
tools.notes: In :vlr-beginClose the drawing is about to be destroyed; do not rely on further LISP execution in that document. The parameter list for :vlr-beginSave contains the target file name.

tools.name: vlr-docmanager-reactor
tools.description: Creates a reactor that notifies of MDI document-manager events: a document being created, becoming current, being activated or deactivated, or about to be destroyed. It is how LISP applications keep per-document state or palettes synchronized when the user switches drawings.

parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: Pairs such as (:vlr-documentCreated . fn), (:vlr-documentBecameCurrent . fn), (:vlr-documentToBeActivated . fn), (:vlr-documentToBeDestroyed . fn).

tools.example:
(defun doc-switched (rea args)
  (princ (strcat "\nNow in: " (vla-get-Name (car args)))))
(vlr-docmanager-reactor nil '((:vlr-documentBecameCurrent . doc-switched)))
tools.notes: The reactor belongs to the namespace that created it; use vlr-set-notification to control whether it fires while its document is not active.

tools.name: vlr-sysvar-reactor
tools.description: Creates an editor reactor that notifies when a system variable is about to change or has changed. Useful for reacting to layout switches (CTAB), current layer changes (CLAYER) or unit changes to update custom UI or enforce settings.

parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: Pairs (:vlr-sysVarWillChange . fn) and/or (:vlr-sysVarChanged . fn); args are (name success-flag).

tools.example:
(defun sv-changed (rea args)
  (if (= (car args) "CLAYER")
    (princ (strcat "\nCurrent layer: " (getvar "CLAYER")))))
(vlr-sysvar-reactor nil '((:vlr-sysVarChanged . sv-changed)))
tools.notes: Changing the same system variable inside its own callback causes recursion; guard with a flag. Many variables change during ordinary commands, so keep callbacks fast.

tools.name: vlr-lisp-reactor
tools.description: Creates an editor reactor that notifies when an AutoLISP expression starts evaluating, ends or is cancelled. Mainly used to track commands implemented in LISP (c: functions), which do not trigger command reactors.

parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: Pairs (:vlr-lispWillStart . fn), (:vlr-lispEnded . fn), (:vlr-lispCancelled . fn); the first arg list holds the expression string.

tools.example:
(defun lisp-start (rea args) (princ (strcat "\nLISP: " (car args))))
(vlr-lisp-reactor nil '((:vlr-lispWillStart . lisp-start)))
tools.notes: Fires for every LISP evaluation from the command line, including menu macros, so keep the handler light.

tools.name: vlr-acdb-reactor
tools.description: Creates a database reactor that notifies when any object is appended to, modified in, erased from or unerased in the drawing database. Unlike object reactors it watches all objects, so it is used for auditing and automatic tagging of new entities.

parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: Pairs such as (:vlr-objectAppended . fn), (:vlr-objectModified . fn), (:vlr-objectErased . fn), (:vlr-objectUnErased . fn); args are (database entity-name).

tools.example:
(defun new-obj (rea args)
  (setq *new-ents* (cons (cadr args) *new-ents*)))
(vlr-acdb-reactor nil '((:vlr-objectAppended . new-obj)))
; process *new-ents* later from a :vlr-commandEnded callback
tools.notes: Very chatty: it fires for every object, including those created internally by commands. Only collect entity names in the callback and do the real work later.

tools.name: vlr-miscellaneous-reactor
tools.description: Creates an editor reactor for events that fit no other category, notably changes to the pickfirst (implied) selection set and switching layouts. It is the hook for tools that react to what the user has selected or to tab changes.

parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: Pairs (:vlr-pickfirstModified . fn) and (:vlr-layoutSwitched . fn).

tools.example:
(defun on-layout (rea args) (princ (strcat "\nLayout: " (car args))))
(vlr-miscellaneous-reactor nil '((:vlr-layoutSwitched . on-layout)))
tools.notes: Inside :vlr-pickfirstModified, (ssget "_I") returns the current implied selection.

tools.name: vlr-mouse-reactor
tools.description: Creates an editor reactor that notifies of a double-click or right-click in the drawing area. It is commonly used to run a custom editor when the user double-clicks a particular block or object type.

parameters.name: callbacks
parameters.description: Pairs (:vlr-beginDoubleClick . fn) and (:vlr-beginRightClick . fn); args contain the WCS point.

tools.example:
(defun dbl (rea args)
  (princ (strcat "\nDouble-click at " (vl-princ-to-string (car args)))))
(vlr-mouse-reactor nil '((:vlr-beginDoubleClick . dbl)))
tools.notes: The built-in double-click action (DBLCLKEDIT / CUI double-click actions) still runs; the CUI Double Click Actions node is often the better tool for simple overrides.

tools.name: vlr-remove
tools.description: Disables a reactor so its callbacks no longer fire. The reactor object still exists and can be re-enabled with vlr-add. Always remove reactors you no longer need, particularly before reloading the code that created them.

parameters.name: reactor
parameters.description: Reactor object returned by a vlr-*-reactor constructor.

tools.example: (if *hatch-rea* (progn (vlr-remove *hatch-rea*) (setq *hatch-rea* nil)))
tools.notes: Returns the reactor, or nil if it was already disabled. vlr-added-p tests whether a reactor is currently enabled.

tools.name: vlr-remove-all
tools.description: Disables all reactors of a given type, or every reactor in the namespace when no type is given. A blunt but useful clean-up during development when reloading code has left duplicate reactors behind.

parameters.name: reactor-type
parameters.description: Type symbol such as :VLR-Command-Reactor or :VLR-Object-Reactor; omit to disable all.

tools.example: (vlr-remove-all :VLR-Command-Reactor)
tools.notes: Also disables reactors created by other applications loaded in the same document namespace, so avoid it in production code.

tools.name: vlr-reactors
tools.description: Returns a list of existing reactors, grouped by type: each sublist starts with the type symbol followed by the reactor objects. With arguments it restricts the result to the given types. Used to find and clean up reactors by their data tag.

parameters.name: reactor-type
parameters.description: Optional type symbols to filter on.

tools.example:
(foreach r (cdar (vlr-reactors :VLR-Object-Reactor))
  (if (= (vlr-data r) "len-watch") (vlr-remove r)))
tools.notes: Pair it with a unique string in the reactor's data argument so your code can identify its own reactors.

tools.name: vlr-add
tools.description: Re-enables a reactor previously disabled with vlr-remove. This allows temporarily muting a reactor while your own code makes changes that would otherwise trigger it.

parameters.name: reactor
parameters.description: A disabled reactor object.

tools.example:
(vlr-remove *mod-rea*)
(vla-put-Color obj acRed)   ; change without triggering our own reactor
(vlr-add *mod-rea*)
tools.notes: Returns the reactor object. vlr-added-p reports the current enabled state.

tools.name: vlr-data
tools.description: Returns the application-specific data stored in a reactor when it was created. Callbacks use it to find associated objects or configuration, and management code uses it to identify reactors. vlr-data-set replaces the data.

parameters.name: reactor
parameters.description: Reactor object.

tools.example:
(defun follow (owner rea args / lbl)
  (setq lbl (vlr-data rea))   ; the label object stored at creation
  (if (not (vlax-erased-p lbl))
    (vla-put-InsertionPoint lbl (vla-get-EndPoint owner))))
tools.notes: Storing a VLA-object in the data of the same reactor that watches it is fine, but do not modify the owner itself in the callback.

tools.name: vlr-pers
tools.description: Makes a reactor persistent, meaning it is saved with the drawing and recreated when the drawing is reopened. The callback functions must be loaded again (for example from acaddoc.lsp) before the reactor can fire in a new session.

parameters.name: reactor
parameters.description: Reactor object (object reactors are the usual candidates).

tools.example:
(setq r (vlr-object-reactor (list ln) "len-watch" '((:vlr-modified . on-mod))))
(vlr-pers r)
; list persistent reactors later: (vlr-pers-list)
tools.notes: If the callback functions are not defined when the drawing opens, events produce errors. vlr-pers-release makes a reactor transient again; vlr-pers-p tests the state.

tools.name: vlr-owner-add
tools.description: Adds an object to the owner list of an existing object reactor, so one reactor can watch many objects. vlr-owner-remove removes an owner and vlr-owners returns the current list.

parameters.name: reactor
parameters.description: An object reactor.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: VLA-object to add as a notifier.

tools.example:
(vlr-owner-add *mod-rea* (vlax-ename->vla-object (entlast)))
(length (vlr-owners *mod-rea*))
tools.notes: Only valid for object reactors. Erased owners stay in the list until removed.

tools.name: vlr-types
tools.description: Returns a list of all reactor type symbols available, such as :VLR-Command-Reactor, :VLR-DWG-Reactor, :VLR-Object-Reactor and :VLR-Mouse-Reactor. vlr-reaction-names lists the events each type supports.

parameters.name: (none)
parameters.description: vlr-types takes no arguments; vlr-reaction-names takes a reactor type symbol.

tools.example:
(vlr-types)
(vlr-reaction-names :VLR-DWG-Reactor)
tools.notes: Types include Linker, Editor, AcDb, DocManager, Command, Lisp, DXF, DWG, Insert, Wblock, SysVar, DeepClone, XREF, Undo, Window, Toolbar, Mouse, Miscellaneous and Object reactors.

tools.name: vlr-reaction-set
tools.description: Adds or replaces the callback function for one event on an existing reactor. It lets code update handlers after reloading, without destroying and recreating reactors that may be persistent.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: Event symbol, e.g. :vlr-commandEnded.

parameters.name: function
parameters.description: Quoted function symbol.

tools.example:
(vlr-reaction-set *cmd-rea* :vlr-commandEnded 'my-cmd-ended-v2)
(vlr-reactions *cmd-rea*)
tools.notes: vlr-reactions returns the current (event . function) pairs of a reactor.

tools.name: vl-doc-set
tools.description: Sets a variable in the namespace of the current document from code running inside a separate-namespace VLX application. It is how a compiled application with its own namespace returns values into the drawing's ordinary LISP environment.

parameters.name: 'symbol
parameters.description: Quoted variable name in the document namespace.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Value to assign.

tools.example:
; inside a separate-namespace VLX
(vl-doc-set '*last-report* "C:/Reports/rooms.csv")
tools.notes: When called from ordinary (document) namespace code it simply behaves like set. vl-doc-ref reads the value back.

tools.name: vl-doc-ref
tools.description: Returns the value of a variable from the current document's namespace, typically called from a separate-namespace VLX that needs to read settings defined in the drawing's LISP environment.

parameters.name: 'symbol
parameters.description: Quoted variable name.

tools.example: (setq scale (vl-doc-ref '*project-scale*))
tools.notes: Each open drawing has its own namespace, so the value can differ between documents.

tools.name: vl-propagate
tools.description: Copies the value of a variable into the namespaces of all open documents and of any drawing opened later in the same session. Used for session-wide settings such as a project path chosen once by the user.

parameters.name: 'symbol
parameters.description: Quoted variable whose current value should be copied everywhere.

tools.example:
(setq *project-root* "P:/2026-017/")
(vl-propagate '*project-root*)
tools.notes: Values are copied, not shared: later changes in one document do not propagate automatically. The blackboard (vl-bb-set / vl-bb-ref) is the alternative for shared state.

tools.name: vl-bb-set
tools.description: Sets a variable in the blackboard namespace, a session-wide namespace shared by all documents. Paired with vl-bb-ref, it is the simple way to pass values between drawings or between a VLX and document code.

parameters.name: 'symbol
parameters.description: Quoted symbol in the blackboard.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Value to store.

tools.example:
(vl-bb-set '*clipboard-layer* (getvar "CLAYER"))
; in another drawing
(setvar "CLAYER" (vl-bb-ref '*clipboard-layer*))
tools.notes: Blackboard variables live only for the session and are not saved in any drawing.

tools.name: vl-load-all
tools.description: Loads a LISP, FAS or VLX file into every open document and into every document opened later in the session. It avoids having to add a file to acaddoc.lsp for code that is loaded on demand.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: File name or path; searched on the support path if no path is given.

tools.example: (vl-load-all "C:/CAD/Lisp/stdtools.lsp")
tools.notes: Subject to SECURELOAD/TRUSTEDPATHS like load. For permanent loading prefer acaddoc.lsp or an autoloader bundle.

tools.name: vlax-get-or-create-object
tools.description: Returns a running instance of a COM application, or starts a new one if none is running, given its ProgID. It is the entry point for driving Excel, Word, the Windows Scripting Host (Scripting.FileSystemObject) or other automation servers from AutoLISP.

parameters.name: ProgID
parameters.description: Programmatic identifier, e.g. "Excel.Application" or "Scripting.FileSystemObject".

tools.example:
(setq xl (vlax-get-or-create-object "Excel.Application"))
(vlax-put-property xl 'Visible :vlax-true)
(setq wb (vlax-invoke-method (vlax-get-property xl 'Workbooks) 'Add))
(vlax-put-property (vlax-get-property (vlax-get-property wb 'ActiveSheet) 'Range "A1") 'Value "Area")
tools.notes: Not supported in AutoCAD LT (no external automation). Release every external object with vlax-release-object. vlax-get-object only attaches to a running instance; vlax-create-object always starts a new one.

tools.name: vlax-import-type-library
tools.description: Imports a COM type library and generates wrapper functions with prefixes you choose (for example msxl- for Excel methods and properties, plus constants). This gives vla-style functions for another application's object model.

parameters.name: :tlb-filename
parameters.description: Path of the .tlb/.olb/.exe/.dll containing the type library.

parameters.name: :methods-prefix / :properties-prefix / :constants-prefix
parameters.description: Prefixes for generated method, property (-get-/-put-) and constant symbols.

tools.example:
(vlax-import-type-library
  :tlb-filename "C:/Program Files/Microsoft Office/root/Office16/EXCEL.EXE"
  :methods-prefix "msxl-" :properties-prefix "msxl-" :constants-prefix "msxl-")
tools.notes: Must be called at top level of a file (not inside a function) and before code that uses the generated names is compiled. Not available in AutoCAD LT. Most developers skip it and use vlax-get-property/vlax-invoke-method directly.

tools.name: vlax-tmatrix
tools.description: Converts a list of four lists (a 4x4 transformation matrix) into the variant form required by ActiveX methods such as TransformBy. It lets matrices obtained from nentselp or computed in LISP be applied to objects.

parameters.name: list-of-4-lists
parameters.description: Four rows of four reals; row 4 is normally (0 0 0 1).

tools.example:
; uniform scale by 2 about the origin
(vla-TransformBy obj (vlax-tmatrix '((2 0 0 0) (0 2 0 0) (0 0 2 0) (0 0 0 1))))
tools.notes: nentselp returns a 4x4 matrix that can be passed directly to vlax-tmatrix to move nested geometry into WCS.

tools.name: vlax-ldata-put
tools.description: Stores LISP data (numbers, strings, lists) in a named drawing dictionary or attached to an object, under a key. The data is saved with the drawing and read back with vlax-ldata-get, making it a simple persistence mechanism for application settings.

parameters.name: dict-or-object
parameters.description: Dictionary name string, or a VLA-object/ename to attach data to.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: String key.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: LISP data to store.

tools.example:
(vlax-ldata-put "MYAPP" "settings" '(("scale" . 50) ("prefix" . "R-")))
(vlax-ldata-put (vlax-ename->vla-object ent) "room-no" "1.07")
tools.notes: LDATA is readable only through AutoLISP; for data other applications must read, use xrecords (entmakex/dictadd) or XData. vlax-ldata-list lists all keys, vlax-ldata-delete removes one, vlax-ldata-test checks whether a value can be stored.

tools.name: vlax-ldata-get
tools.description: Retrieves LISP data stored with vlax-ldata-put from a drawing dictionary or an object, returning a default value if the key is absent.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: String key used when storing.

parameters.name: default-data
parameters.description: Value returned when the key does not exist.

tools.example:
(setq cfg (vlax-ldata-get "MYAPP" "settings" '(("scale" . 100))))
(cdr (assoc "scale" cfg))
tools.notes: The private flag lets a separate-namespace VLX keep data that other namespaces cannot read.

tools.name: vlax-add-cmd
tools.description: Registers an AutoLISP function as a native AutoCAD command without the c: prefix, optionally as a transparent command and with control over pickfirst behaviour. Commands defined this way behave more like ObjectARX commands, for example they can be invoked transparently.

parameters.name: global-name
parameters.description: Command name string.

parameters.name: func-sym
parameters.description: Symbol of a function taking no arguments.

parameters.name: local-name
parameters.description: Localized name; defaults to global-name.

parameters.name: cmd-flags
parameters.description: ACRX_CMD_MODAL (0) or ACRX_CMD_TRANSPARENT (1), plus ACRX_CMD_USEPICKSET (2) or ACRX_CMD_REDRAW (4); default is modal + redraw.

tools.example:
(defun show-area () (princ (strcat "\nArea: " (rtos (getvar "AREA") 2 2))) (princ))
(vlax-add-cmd "SHOWAREA" 'show-area "SHOWAREA" ACRX_CMD_TRANSPARENT)
; usable as 'SHOWAREA inside another command
tools.notes: A transparently defined command cannot call (command). The function must not create reactors or serve as a reactor callback. vlax-remove-cmd unregisters it. Loading from a separate-namespace VLX via APPLOAD is recommended.
